full_name: Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence
mission: CFI is an interdisciplinary Cambridge research centre, funded by the Leverhulme Trust and launched in 2016 by Stephen Hawking, that studies the nature, ethics and impact of AI. It brings together machine learning, philosophy, history, literature and design to study AI's risks and opportunities in the short and long term. Its AI: Futures and Responsibility programme, run with CSER, focuses on extreme risks and governance.

key_work.title: AI: Futures and Responsibility (AI:FAR) programme
key_work.plain_summary: Research on the long-term and extreme risks of AI and how governance — including US–China cooperation — can reduce them.

key_work.title: Kinds of Intelligence programme
key_work.plain_summary: Studies how AI compares with human and animal minds, including how to evaluate AI capabilities and questions about AI consciousness.

key_work.title: AI: Narratives and Justice programme
key_work.plain_summary: Examines the stories we tell about AI and how they shape who benefits and who is harmed.

status_raw: active — part of Cambridge's Institute for Technology and Humanity (ITH) with CSER

people.role: Associate Director (Research Strategy); Programme Director, AI:FAR

warnings.text: The rise of powerful AI will be either the best or the worst thing ever to happen to humanity (Stephen Hawking, at CFI's launch).
AI can amplify injustice and be used in automated warfare.

recommendations.text: Study AI across disciplines, not just computer science.
Pursue international cooperation, including between the West and China, on AI safety.
Educate future leaders through dedicated AI ethics and society programmes.
